name: readthrough
code_version_note: the commit at build time, which precedes the commit that lands this file

inputs.role: Toledano et al., Nat Genet 56:1914-1924 (2024), PMID 39174735, supplementary table 3: 5,837 measured premature stop codons x 8 compounds, as percent of the no-PTC control. Gitignored under build/: a rebuildable download, not a source file
the case's stop codon, its +4 and -1 bases and its NMD verdict (gitignored: the file holds transcript offsets)

controls.panel: the named benchmark panel, held out of the fit before any run

assumptions: readthrough measured in a HEK293T fluorescent reporter, with 144 nt of native context around the stop, transfers to the same stop in its own gene in the child's tissues; the stop codon, its +4 base and its -1 base capture the part of the context that generalises
limitations: one cell line, one assay, one concentration per compound; 431 of 52,062 values are censored at the assay ceiling and are read as their lower bound, so the means are lower bounds; the untreated column sits at the assay floor (~0.18 %), so any prediction near it is noise rather than a small effect; reporter readthrough is not functional protein rescue, which also needs the message to survive NMD and the near-cognate amino acid to be tolerated at that position; nothing has been measured in this child
validation: every drug's row carries its own held-out control, on a benchmark panel named before the run and on a random fifth of contexts; a row whose control failed is not interpretable as a prediction. The dataset's own untreated column runs through the identical pipeline as a negative control and must fail

sources.genomic: the child's own callset, read only as: gene, consequence class, and the coding-sequence offset of the stop, which is used inside build/ to derive the codon and its context. No genomic position appears in any row
sources.clinical: the proband's 8 HPO terms (Challenge_Clinical_Phenotype_1.md), used to decide which adverse-effect axes disqualify a candidate: nephrocalcinosis HP:0000121 against aminoglycoside tubular nephrotoxicity, failure to thrive HP:0001508 and short stature HP:0004322 against chronic parenteral dosing, rhabdomyosarcoma HP:0002859 against agents whose class is cytotoxic or which stabilise oncogenic nonsense transcripts
sources.public: Ensembl REST release 116 (gene model, coding sequence), UniProt O60566 (domains), Toledano et al. Nat Genet 2024 PMID 39174735 supplementary table 3 (measured readthrough), and the BubR1 dosage literature cited per row

columns.predicted_readthrough: percent of the no-PTC control, the unit the source dataset reports
columns.evidence_level: which backoff level answered: stop+4-1, stop+4, stop, or drug
columns.rows_behind_it: measured contexts in that cell of the full fit (the control refits without the panel)
columns.control_passed: the declared benchmark-panel control for this drug; false means the row is not interpretable as a number
columns.contexts_behind_it: up to six example PTC contexts from the cell, so a reader can spot-check the group

clinical_framing: research exercise; no row advises for or against giving any drug to any patient
patient_data: none in this file. Sequence-derived facts are stated as codon identity, exon index, counts and fractions; no genomic position and no run of patient sequence appears
